synopsis: Applied Intuition is a commercial, road-derived simulation platform adapted for mining, construction and agriculture; its advertised toolchain spans scenario, sensor and vehicle-dynamics simulation, HIL and large-scale cloud execution, while its data platforms ingest logs and manage regression testing [f8964, f8683, f8396, f8658]. It acquired CarSim and TruckSim through Mechanical Simulation in March 2022 and launched an off-road autonomy stack on 17 June 2024 [f8402, f8397]. A multi-year Komatsu partnership announced on 9 September 2025 covers Vehicle OS, autonomous haulage and collision avoidance for staffed sites, including planned EMESRT control level 9 systems; this provides independent evidence of off-road relevance, but independent validation of automatic braking on heavy machines was not found [f8399, f8400, f8684, f8289]. Applied Intuition's R171 blog describes physical tests as expected, with virtual testing permitted for certain difficult-to-reproduce scenarios subject to rigorous toolchain credibility evaluation [f1277, f1278]. Planning gaps include unavailable public pricing, an unverified interface/standards picture, no detailed public sensor matrix and no sensor-model validation evidence for dust, snow or soil; raw-data compatibility must therefore be checked against the eventual sensors [f8405, f8968, f8403, f8407, f8659]. Reported acceleration and productivity gains are marketing rather than independent or controlled cross-vendor benchmarks, and supplying both validation tools and autonomy stacks creates a potential competitive conflict for manufacturers developing their own perception and braking functions [f8406, f8735, f8409].
